prepare.title: Prepare ahead
prepare.link: Prepare ahead: turn on your phone's own SOS →
prepare.intro: Most phones have their own Emergency SOS. When it is on, pressing a button a few times can send your location to your people, even without opening SafeConnect. On many phones this also calls the emergency number (999). Below are the official steps for the companies where we found them.
check: Turn on your phone's SOS (find your phone's company below).
Save your people's numbers: in the phone's SOS and in SafeConnect.
Check once: see that the settings are right, and tell your people.
prepare.warn: Never test by calling 999 or by starting SOS. If an emergency call goes out by mistake, don't hang up: tell the operator it was a mistake.
prepare.none: We found no instructions on this company's official help pages, so we don't name any menu. See the phone's manual or ask the company's service centre.
prepare.unread: The company has an official page, but we could not open it to check, so we list no steps. See the instructions at the link below.
prepare.note: Phone companies can change their menus. If it doesn't match, see the company's page.

apple.name: iPhone (Apple)
steps: Go to Settings > Emergency SOS and turn on “Call with 5 Presses”.
Add Emergency Contacts in the Health app.
When an emergency call ends, your iPhone texts your emergency contacts with your location (if available).

samsung.name: Samsung
steps: Open Settings > Safety and emergency > Emergency SOS.
Turn on “Send SOS to emergency contacts” and add your people with Add contacts.
Pressing the Side button five times in a row starts SOS.
samsung.note: Samsung's page says the phone needs an active SIM card to send an SOS alert.

pixel.name: Google Pixel
steps: In Settings > Safety and emergency > Emergency SOS, tap Start setup.
To share your location, add your people with Add contact.
Pressing the power button five times or more starts SOS.
pixel.note: Google's page says Emergency SOS doesn't work in airplane mode or when Battery Saver is on.

xiaomi.name: Xiaomi / Redmi
steps: Open Settings > Safety & emergency > Emergency SOS.
Turn on “Share info with emergency contacts”: your location is shared when SOS starts.
Pressing the power button quickly five times or more starts SOS.
xiaomi.note: Xiaomi's official page does not say how to add emergency contacts.

prepare.liveTitle: Turn on live location (WhatsApp or Google Maps)
prepare.liveWhy: SafeConnect's message sends your location once, at the moment you send it. WhatsApp and Google Maps keep sending it for the time you choose, even after you close SafeConnect. This needs internet.
waSteps: Open the chat of the person you want to send to.
Tap Attach (📎) > Location > Share live location.
Choose how long, then tap Send.
mapsSteps: Open Google Maps and tap your profile picture.
Choose the time and the people, then tap Share.

page.welcomeTitle: Welcome! First time here? Three things to know:
welcomeSteps: Tap "Find help near me" to see the numbers of your police station and chairman.
Save your family's numbers now, so you can send your location quickly.

page.guideText: Pick your situation and we will show you who to call.
guides: In danger at night or on the road
Call 999 first. Then send your location to your family.
File a General Diary (GD) at the nearest police station. Find your police station number here.
Fire service {fire}, disaster warning {warn}. See your upazila numbers too.
duo: In an emergency there is no time to look for numbers. Save them once and you can send your location quickly. No login.
On an area page, every number has "Report a wrong number" (you need to sign in). We check it against the official source and fix it if it is wrong.

emergency.call999Sub: Police, fire service, ambulance · free, 24 hours

danger.title: In danger
do: Call 999 now and say where you are.
If you can, go to a crowded or well-lit place.
Send your family the danger message with the big button above.

followed.title: Someone is following me
do: Go to a crowded or well-lit place, go into a shop.
Call 999.
Send your family the danger message (a message, not a call).
Keep the nearest police station's number at hand.

accident.title: Accident
do: Call 999 and say the place.
Better not to move the injured person; move them carefully only if there is fire or traffic danger.
If there is bleeding, press a clean cloth on it.
Take them to the nearest hospital and tell the police.

sick.title: Medical emergency
do: If it is serious, call 999 now and ask for an ambulance.
Doctor's advice: Health Call Centre 16263 (24 hours).
See the nearest hospital or pharmacy with the buttons below.
Send your family the danger message.

lost.title: Lost
do: Stay where you are; look for the names of nearby shops or the bazar.
Send your family your location (the big button above).
Tourists: the Tourist Police number is in the helplines below.

harassment.title: Harassment
do: Move to a safe place and tell the people around you.
Violence against women and children: call 109 (free, 24 hours).
If the danger grows, call 999 now.

about.title: What is SafeConnect?
about.text: In an emergency, finding the right number takes time you do not have. SafeConnect uses your location to show the official numbers for your police station, union council, village police and hospital, in the order to call them. All over Bangladesh.
points: Every number comes from an official *.gov.bd website, with its source link. The sources are re-checked every week.
After one visit, the numbers, area search, "Find help near me" and sending your location by SMS work without internet.
Your family's numbers stay on your phone. We collect no personal data.

faq.title: Good to know
items: Where do the numbers come from?
From the official websites (*.gov.bd) of districts, upazilas, unions and municipalities. Each number shows its source link and the date the source was checked.
What if a number is wrong?
On an area page, tap "Report a wrong number" under the number (you need to sign in). We check it against the official source and fix it if it is wrong. In an emergency, call 999 first.

Yes. Open the site once with internet; after that all numbers, area search, "Find help near me" and SMS work without internet. Only WhatsApp, maps, source links and reporting a wrong number need internet. Calls and SMS still need mobile signal.

Nowhere. Your family's numbers and last area stay in your phone's browser. Your location is sent only when you send it. If you turn on "Update my area automatically", your location is checked on this phone only, and only the area name is saved.
What if I use someone else's phone, or a phone the family shares?

Your family's numbers and saved areas stay only on this phone, so anyone who uses the phone can see them. To delete a number, tap "Remove" next to it on the "Send location" page. If you signed in on someone else's phone, tick "Also remove my family's numbers and saved areas from this phone" when you sign out. Calling 999 works as before.
Does it work in every district?

Yes, in all 64 districts. Hospitals, police stations, pharmacies and 9 more kinds of places are shown everywhere. Official area numbers are being added step by step; where they are not added yet, it shows 999 and the nearest police station and hospital. National numbers like 999, 109 and 333 work everywhere.

foot.tagline: Official emergency numbers for your area. No login; works without internet too.
foot.helpText: For information about any government service, call 333. To tell us about this project, write on GitHub.
foot.credit: Numbers: official *.gov.bd websites. Map: upazila boundaries and union/town centre points from the Bangladesh Bureau of Statistics (BBS) via OCHA HDX (CC BY-IGO). Where BBS names do not match, the tools can add OpenStreetMap points (© OpenStreetMap contributors, ODbL).
